THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL: 15 RULERS MOSES → SAMUEL
ACCESSION
How Moses came to power
Forty years before his call, a Hebrew had refused him: "Who made thee a prince and a judge over us?" Exodus 2:14 Acts 7:23–30
At Horeb, from the burning bush, God sent him: "I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people". Exodus 3:1–2 Exodus 3:10–12
Moses said he was "slow of speech"; God gave him Aaron as spokesman: "thou shalt be to him instead of God". Exodus 4:10–16
Moses and Aaron gathered the elders; the people believed and worshipped. Exodus 4:29–31
He was eighty when he and Aaron spoke to Pharaoh. Exodus 7:7
SUCCESSION
Before and after
ON THE WORLD STAGE: Egypt · Amalek · Edom and Moab · The Amorite kings · Midian
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
Stephen calls him the man whom Israel refused as "a ruler and a judge", and whom God sent "to be a ruler and a deliverer". Acts 7:35
"Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth." Numbers 12:3
God speaks with Moses "mouth to mouth", and calls him faithful "in all mine house". Numbers 12:7–8 Hebrews 3:5
"There arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face." Deuteronomy 34:10–12
Moses stood "in the breach" to turn God's wrath from the people. Psalms 106:23 Exodus 32:30–32
Later Scripture remembers the Exodus as led "by the hand of Moses and Aaron", with Miriam sent before the people too. Psalms 77:20 Micah 6:4
"The law was given by Moses." John 1:17
At Meribah Moses struck the rock and said "must we fetch you water"; God told him he would not bring the people into the land. Numbers 20:10–12 Numbers 27:12–14
The Psalms say "it went ill with Moses for their sakes", because "he spake unadvisedly with his lips". Psalms 106:32–33
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points

THE LAND
The places Scripture names
The tribes of Israel · tribe of Levi. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
THE NATION
What the nation did
The people answered "All the words which the LORD hath said will we do", and the covenant was sealed with blood. Exodus 24:3–8
They made a molten calf while Moses was on the mountain; about three thousand died that day. Exodus 32:15–20 Exodus 32:25–29
PROPHETS
Prophets of the reign
Aa Aaron “See, I have made thee a god to Pharaoh: and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.”
Mi Miriam Miriam "the prophetess" led the women after the crossing of the sea; Micah names her with Moses and Aaron as sent before the people.

El Eldad and Medad Two men who "were of them that were written" stayed in the camp, and the spirit rested on them there; when Joshua said "forbid them", Moses answered "would God that all the LORD's people were prophets".

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S OWN NUMBERS
No years given

Scripture gives Moses' ages (80 when he spoke to Pharaoh, 120 at his death) and forty years of leadership, but no year BC. The two dates below are scholars' reconstructions of the Exodus, not of Moses' life.
EARLY EXODUS (1 KINGS 6:1 COUNTED BACK)
Mack (ISBE, 1915) counts the 480 years of 1 Kings 6:1 back from Solomon's temple and puts the Exodus about 1448 BC.
EXODUS UNDER MERENPTAH
Driver (1911) places the Exodus under Pharaoh Merenptah; these are that pharaoh's years on Petrie's dates, not the years of Moses' leadership.
Two different bodies; Deuteronomy 1 retells Exodus 18
Keil (1871 and 1872 translations)
Keil reads Deuteronomy 1:12–18 as Moses' own account of the Exodus 18 appointment, and the seventy elders as a separate council given the Spirit to help Moses govern.[15][16]
One institution told in different sources
Knobel and the critics from Vater onward, as reported by Keil

These critics identified the seventy elders with the judges of Exodus 18 and took Deuteronomy 1:9–18 to refer to both, using the differences as evidence of separate documents. Keil reports and rejects this.[16]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no year BC for Moses or the Exodus, and never names the Pharaoh he faced.

Scripture gives Moses no fixed title for his office. It calls him "the servant of the LORD" and a prophet, and Stephen calls him "a ruler and a deliverer" (Deuteronomy 34:5, 34:10; Acts 7:35). Whether Deuteronomy 33:5 calls him king is disputed.
Moses' sons held no office of rule. They "were named of the tribe of Levi" (1 Chronicles 23:14-15), and the leadership passed to Joshua of Ephraim.
Nothing more is recorded of the seventy elders after Numbers 11.
